options: The angle between two vectors, ignoring their magnitude, ranging from -1 to 1
The total number of dimensions two vectors share
The straight-line distance between two points
How many words two pieces of text have in common
questions.explain: Cosine similarity isolates direction by dividing out magnitude, producing a bounded score from -1 (opposite) to 1 (identical direction).

questions.q: In this lesson's worked example with A = [1, 2, 3] and B = [2, 4, 5], what is the dot product A · B?
questions.explain: A · B = (1x2) + (2x4) + (3x5) = 2 + 8 + 15 = 25, as computed step by step in the lesson.

questions.q: Why can dot product alone be misleading when comparing embedding vectors?
options: A vector with larger magnitude (length) can produce a higher dot product without actually pointing in a more similar direction
Dot product can only be computed on vectors with fewer than 10 dimensions
Dot product is always identical to Euclidean distance
Dot product cannot be computed for negative numbers
questions.explain: Because dot product is sensitive to vector length, a longer vector can inflate the score even when it isn't semantically closer — which is exactly why cosine similarity divides that out.

questions.q: What does Euclidean distance measure, and how does 'more similar' read on its scale?
options: The angle between two vectors; higher values mean more similar
The straight-line distance between the two vector points; lower values mean more similar
The dot product normalized by vector length; higher values mean more similar
The number of matching dimensions; higher values mean more similar
questions.explain: Unlike cosine similarity and dot product, Euclidean distance works in the opposite direction — a smaller distance means the two points (and the text they represent) are more alike.

questions.q: Why do many vector databases default to dot product instead of cosine similarity?
options: Dot product is more accurate than cosine similarity in every case
Cosine similarity cannot be used for retrieval tasks
Once every vector is L2-normalized to length 1, dot product and cosine similarity produce identical rankings, and dot product is cheaper to compute
Dot product requires less storage space than cosine similarity
questions.explain: When vectors are pre-normalized to unit length, the magnitude term that distinguishes dot product from cosine similarity becomes irrelevant, so dot product gives the same ranking at a lower computational cost.
